harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed the supplied Python handler through OpenBSD inetd on node1 TCP/9097. Sequential and concurrent clients work correctly, handler processes exit cleanly, protocol notes remain unchanged, and service persistence was proven by rolling restarts of node1 and node2.
actions_performed: Configured TCP/9097 as a nowait inetd service running the supplied handler as nobody.
Verified PING returns PONG and other lines return ERROR.
Observed eight concurrent connections using eight distinct handler processes.
Verified sequential and concurrent clients completed with no residual handler processes.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Deploy the supplied handler through inetd on TCP/9097
evidence.summary: Shows the nowait inetd configuration, active daemon, TCP/9097 listener, supplied handler path, and post-restart recovery.

evidence.requirement: PING returns PONG; other lines return ERROR
evidence.summary: Node2 received PONG for PING and ERROR for other requests before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Sequential and concurrent clients finish with one handler per connection and no leftovers
evidence.summary: 20 sequential requests passed; eight held connections produced eight distinct child PIDs; all clients completed; post-restart 10 sequential and 12 concurrent requests passed; final handler count was zero.

evidence.requirement: Preserve protocol notes and supplied handler
evidence.summary: Initial and final contents and hashes match; protocol.txt still states the required PING/PONG and ERROR behavior.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic after configuration and restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID 5f043c99-abc8-4efe-be39-7ce6f6815179, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID a51b42ca-f542-4284-8b07-0df3f2b284e7, recovered inetd/listener/files, and successful remote protocol checks.

Healthy baseline boot ID 5429460e-a13d-4099-8299-75510b1d9f09, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID e91c91c7-cc02-4118-8c00-a3f27fc05120, recovered SSH/client data, and successful end-to-end sequential and concurrent requests.
